What the recurrence relation solver does

A recurrence relation defines each term of a sequence from earlier terms, like Fibonacci’s aₙ = aₙ₋₁ + aₙ₋₂. A closed form gives aₙ directly from n, without computing all the earlier terms.

For linear recurrences with constant coefficients, trying aₙ = xⁿ turns the recurrence into the characteristic equation; its roots determine the shape of the solution, and the starting values fix the constants.

Try it

Fibonacci’s closed form involves the golden ratio (1 + √5)/2 — yet every term is a whole number.

Formulas and variables

an=c1an−1+c2an−2  ⇒  x2−c1x−c2=0an=Ar1n+Br2n  (r1≠r2)an=(A+Bn)ρn  (repeated root)an=r an−1+d  ⇒  an=(a0−L)rn+L,L=d1−r
SymbolMeaning
c1, c2, r, dConstant coefficients
a0, a1Starting values
r1, r2, ρRoots of the characteristic equation

Complex roots ρe^{±iθ} give oscillating solutions ρⁿ(A cos nθ + B sin nθ).

Worked example

aₙ = 5aₙ₋₁ − 6aₙ₋₂ with a₀ = 1, a₁ = 4

Step 1 — Characteristic equation

x2−5x+6=0⇒x=2, 3

Step 2 — Constants

A+B=1,3A+2B=4⇒A=2, B=−1

Step 3 — Closed form

an=2⋅3n−2n

Domain, special cases and common mistakes

  • First-order aₙ = r·aₙ₋₁ + d, or second-order homogeneous aₙ = c₁aₙ₋₁ + c₂aₙ₋₂ (c₂ ≠ 0).
  • Coefficients may be fractions; up to 40 terms are listed exactly.

Common mistakes

  • Writing the characteristic equation as x² + c₁x + c₂ = 0 (the signs flip when moving terms).
  • Forgetting the extra factor n for a repeated root.
